question: to the Commission César Luena (S&D), Hana Jalloul Muro (S&D), José Cepeda (S&D) Subject:

The Assembly of Madrid has adopted a hunting and fishing law that includes population control plans for species with surplus animals – which can also be used outside normal hunting periods – expands the use of certain hunting technologies and amends the rules for various huntable species. A number of scientific and environmental organisations have questioned the scientific basis of some of these measures and have raised concerns about their potential impact on biodiversity. As wildlife management must comply with the Birds and Habitats Directives, could the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it consider that measures like these should be based on up-to-date scientific information on the conservation status of the species concerned, which would provide justification for their necessity, proportionality and compatibility with the conservation objectives set out in both Directives?

What obligations under those Directives must be fulfilled when adopting rules that expand, or change the purpose of, hunting for wild species, such as authorising population control outside normal hunting periods or expanding the tools used to that end?
How does the Commission verify whether this type of regional legislative reform is compatible with the EU’s species and habitats conservation objectives?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2026) The Birds1 and the Habitats2 Directives require that hunting and fishing and any population management of wild species covered by these Directives respect the objective of maintaining or restoring favourable conservation status. The case-law of the Court of Justice of the European Union underscores the importance of using the best available scientific information as a basis for implementing the Directives. Hunting and fishing regimes as well as population control measures must be aligned with the Directives’ protection systems3. Species listed in Annex V of the Habitats Directive and Annex II of the Birds Directive may be hunted and subject to management measures, if this is compatible with their being maintained at a favourable conservation status, and following the provisions set under the Directives. Any derogations from the general provisions, including for strictly protected species, must satisfy the strict and cumulative conditions set out under Article 9 of the Birds Directive and Article 16 of the Habitats Directive (including that there is no other satisfactory solution, that the measure pursues a permitted derogation objective, and that it is subject to strict supervision, selective application and to the other safeguards required by those provisions). The primary responsibility for ensuring that national hunting and fisheries law complies with the applicable EU law lies with the Member States’ competent authorities and judiciary system. In order to assist them, the Commission has adopted several guidance documents4. The Commission, as guardian of the Treaties, monitors the implementation of the EU legislation in EU Member States and may take actions to address systemic non-compliance, when appropriate.
1 Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the

conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7–25. 2 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50. 3 Articles 12 to 16 of the Habitats Directive and Article 7 to 9 of the Birds Directive. 4 Guidance to sustainable hunting under the Birds Directive https://circabc.europa.eu/ui/group/3f466d71-92a749eb-9c63-6cb0fadf29dc/library/c899b11c-90f6-4aad-95c5-aac35e4c1e38/details; Guidance document on the general system of protection of bird species - Article 5 and Article 9 of the Birds Directive https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/guidance-document-general-system-protection-birdspecies-article-5-and-article-9-birds-directive_en; Commission notice Guidance document on the strict protection of animal species of Community interest under the Habitats Directive https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=PI_COM:C(2021)7301; https://environment.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-adopts-guidance-natura-2000-and-fishing-2025-10-17_en.
